text:
maya: Anyone else seeing `redwoodctl login` fail inside WSL2 after the Windows install? Browser pops, I auth, then CLI prints 'no credentials found' and exits. :confused:

raj: Hmm. Did you install via winget on Windows or `curl | bash` inside WSL?

maya: Winget on Windows (so binary lives in C:\Program Files). I usually just call it from WSL PATH (auto-mounted).

sam: That usually breaks stuff because the Windows binary can't access Linux home for the credential cache. What does `which redwoodctl` show inside WSL?

maya: Shows `/mnt/c/Program Files/Redwood/redwoodctl.exe`.

julia: Ah yeah, `redwoodctl` expects to write `~/.config/redwood/credentials` (or use OS cred helper). Windows exe can't write to Linux home reliably.

maya: Error snippet I see:
```
$ redwoodctl login
Opening browser for auth...
Login successful in browser.
Error: failed to read credential helper: exit status 1
```

raj: Two options: install a native Linux binary in WSL, or use a credential helper that both sides can talk to. We recommend native WSL install for best DX.

maya: Tried manually putting a symlink in `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl -> /mnt/c/Program Files/Redwood/redwoodctl.exe` but then `redwoodctl local serve` crashes with permission errors.

sam: Symlink to a Windows exe will behave weirdly. Try installing the Linux build inside WSL: `curl -sSL https://dl.redwood.ai/redwoodctl/linux-amd64/latest.tar.gz | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin` (that's what worked for me).

maya: Do we have an official install snippet for WSL in docs? The one on the website only mentions Homebrew / winget / apt.

ops-bot: Docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/redwoodctl#install (internal note: WSL section planned) :memo:

julia: Workaround if you must use Windows install: set `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=/mnt/c/Users/<you>/.redwood` before login so creds are written to a Windows path both binaries can access. Not ideal but works.

maya: That actually let me login, thanks. But `redwoodctl profiles list` showed an empty profile set until I copied `profiles.json` into that dir. So profiles aren't automatically migrated.

raj: Yep, profiles and local runtime state live in the config dir. Migration isn't automatic across OS boundary. We'll add a note in the WSL troubleshooting doc.

sam: Another thing: browser-based auth sometimes times out because the Windows browser opens but the callback tries to hit 127.0.0.1 inside WSL vs Windows net. If you see a timeout, try `--headless` to use a device code flow: `redwoodctl login --device`

maya: `--device` worked great. Can we add a short FAQ in the onboarding guide: recommended WSL install + `--device` fallback?

julia: Agreed. Filing a docs ticket now.

sam: Also, for local testing, `redwoodctl local serve --config ./redwood.local.yaml` will fail if the socket path points to Windows paths. Use unix socket under `/tmp` in WSL.

maya: Good to know. Thanks all. Filing a quick internal note for the onboarding checklist: recommend native WSL install, `--device` option, and note about profiles migration. :+1:

ops-bot: Created ticket DOCS-1123 for WSL install + auth FAQ (assigned to julia).
